newsitem.title: USA: Justice Dept. joins probe of Maine nuclear reactor.
newsitem.headline: Justice Dept. joins probe of Maine nuclear reactor.

text.p: The Justice Department will review the results of an investigation of the Maine Yankee nuclear plant, but regulators and plant officials cautioned Thursday that this review did not mean wrongdoing had been found.

The Nuclear Regulatory Commission asked Justice Department officials to review its probe of allegations that engineers fraudulently manipulated a computer code used to test a key plant cooling system during the 1980s.

"It is not unusual for the NRC to seek a Justice Department review in high profile cases such as this one. It is our understanding that it represents a continuation of the review process," Maine Yankee general counsel Mary Ann Lunch said in a written statement.

Officials of the plant in Wiscasset, Maine, have denied engineers did anything improper during the tests of the emergency core cooling system, but new tests were submitted to the NRC this year using a different computer model.
The 24-year-old plant has been limited to operating at 90 percent of its 910-megawatt capacity while the new tests are reviewed.

The findings from the probe have not been made public, and while the Justice Department would prosecute if any allegations are taken to court, NRC spokesman Roger Hannah said people should "not read anything" into the request for review.
"That's doesn't mean there has been wrongdoing. It's too early to speculate at this point," Hannah told Maine Public Radio.

The allegations about the testing were originally made in an anonymous letter that provided substantial technical data to support the charges. The author claimed to be a long-time employee of one of Maine Yankee's consultants.

The NRC's inspector general, Leo Norton, ruled in May that regulators failed to review adequately an analysis of the 1980s tests and did not do follow-up checks to see if the plant was following safety requirements.
Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co., 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities and 22 percent by other New England utilities.
